user.title: Set up remotes
user.description: Enter the names of your remotes (device_name from ESPHome, comma separated). Keep the key as is.

fertig.title: Almost done – ESPHome secrets
fertig.description:
ESPHomeRemote needs these lines in the ESPHome **Secrets**:

```yaml
{block}
```

With the tick below they are **added for you** – lines that already exist stay untouched. Only Wi-Fi (`wifi_ssid`, `wifi_password`) you add yourself if it is not there yet (ESPHome add-on → top right **"Secrets"**). Prefer doing it by hand? Remove the tick and copy the block.

Next: flash the remote (or install it once more if it already runs this firmware). Afterwards you find **"Remote"** in the sidebar.

data.eintragen: Add the missing lines to the ESPHome secrets (recommended)

hinweis.title: Home Assistant without ESPHome add-on
hinweis.description: This Home Assistant runs without Supervisor (Container or Core), so there is no ESPHome add-on. ESPHomeRemote works anyway – configurator, key layouts, menu, dock, entities – but it cannot build or flash firmware for you. You build the device files in `{ordner}` with your own ESPHome (`esphome run` with the device file). Continue to set up the integration.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Already set up. Add more remotes via "Configure".

error.schreiben: Could not write the ESPHome secrets file – copy the block by hand.

init.title: Remotes
init.description: Remote names (device_name, comma separated). Key for the ESPHome secrets: `{key}`

data_description.kanal: stabil: releases for everyone. beta: new versions a few days earlier, for testing – the device files are switched to the beta branch on GitHub, and HACS shows betas only if you enable "Show beta versions" for ESPHomeRemote.

to_remotes.name: To all remotes
to_remotes.description: Calls an ESPHome service on all connected remotes (esphome.[remote]_[service]).

service.name: Service
service.description: Part after the device name, e.g. refresh_cover, doorbell_image, remote_show_keyboard

rules.name: Adjust step by step
rules.description: For keys and follow modes of the remote: light brighter/darker, colour temperature, fan speed, toggle oscillation.

step.name: Step
step.description: Brightness in %, colour temperature in Kelvin, fan in steps (negative = down/warmer)

remote_log.name: Remote log via the dock
remote_log.description: Called by the dock when a remote without its own HA connection radios its log (only with debug log on). Errors and warnings go to the HA log, all lines to the configurator.

wifi_coming.name: Remote turns on its Wi-Fi
wifi_coming.description: Called by the dock when a remote is about to turn on its Wi-Fi (voice to HA, no dock). HA then connects as soon as it is reachable.

remote_status.name: Remote values via the dock
remote_status.description: Called by the dock when a remote without its own HA connection radios its values (battery, charging cable, activity, deep sleep status, key configuration). Writes them to the remote's entities while it isn't connected itself.

timer_extend.name: Extend timer
timer_extend.description: Restarts the last finished timer (from the remotes' selection) with this duration – for the “+5 min” button in the timer popup.

timer_restart.name: Restart timer
timer_restart.description: Restarts the last finished timer with its previous duration (“Again” button in the timer popup).

blaster_send.name: Send via another IR/RF transmitter
blaster_send.description: Sends a raw code via an IR transmitter of another integration (infrared entity) or a Broadlink (IR or 433 MHz) – like a dock. The remotes call this for transmitters chosen instead of a dock in the configurator.

code.name: Code
code.description: Times in microseconds, + on / - off, comma-separated

light.name: Control lights (light widget)
light.description: Operation of the remote's light widget: switches, dims, sets colour temperature or colour per light only as far as it supports, or activates a scene.

action.name: Action
action.description: on, off, toggle, brightness, kelvin, color or scene

value.name: Value
value.description: brightness: percent, kelvin: e.g. 2700, color: hue,saturation (e.g. 30,100), scene: scene.xyz

camera_tv.name: Camera on the TV
camera_tv.description: Shows a camera as picture-in-picture on the TV (Configurator > Features), or hides it.

size.name: Size (this time only)
size.description: Optional – small, medium, large or almost_full. Empty = Configurator setting.

position.name: Corner (this time only)
position.description: Optional – top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left or center.

seconds.name: Display time (this time only)
seconds.description: Optional – hide after this many seconds, 0 = until "off". Empty = Configurator setting.

toggle.name: Toggle
toggle.description: If a camera is already showing on this TV, hide it instead (one key for on/off).

camera_size.name: Camera size on the TV
camera_size.description: small, medium, large, almost_full or "next" (cycle). A running camera takes the new size immediately.

camera_position.name: Camera corner on the TV
camera_position.description: Corner of the camera (top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, center) or "next" (clockwise). A running camera moves immediately.

restart.name: Restart device (ADB)
restart.description: Restarts an Android device that is entered in the configurator under Features.

device.name: Device
device.description: Name as in the configurator (e.g. Streamer)

streamer_cec.name: Switch a TV device via HDMI
streamer_cec.description: Turns the soundbar/AV receiver (or the TV) on or off via HDMI-CEC through a streamer.

streamer.name: Streamer
streamer.description: ID or name of the streamer in the Configurator

device.name: Device
device.description: soundbar (audio system on HDMI-ARC) or tv

streamer_menu.name: TV menu
streamer_menu.description: Opens or closes the popup menu of a streamer (Streamer app 1.18+; page, size and position 1.19+).

streamer.name: Streamer
streamer.description: ID or name of the streamer in the Configurator

page.name: Page
page.description: Optional – ID of a menu page to show right away (e.g. camera). Always opens.

size.name: Size (this time only)
size.description: Optional – percent of the screen (30–100, 100 = full screen). Empty = Configurator setting.

position.name: Position (this time only)
position.description: Optional – center, left, right, top, bottom or a corner. Empty = Configurator setting.

allow_actions.title: {name} may not perform Home Assistant actions
allow_actions.description: Keys, menu entries and dock commands of {name} call Home Assistant actions. Open Settings → Devices & services → ESPHome → {name} → Configure and turn on "Allow the device to perform Home Assistant actions".

bridge_address.title: {name} does not point to the Bluetooth bridge
bridge_address.description: The ESPHome entry of {name} connects to {now}. With the developer setup (tools/remotes.json) Home Assistant reaches this remote through the Bluetooth bridge at {host}, port {port}. Either open the ESPHome configurator → Firmware and press "Point ESPHome entries to the bridge", or open Settings → Devices & services → ESPHome → {name} → ⋮ → Reconfigure and enter host {host} and port {port}. If you want this remote to stay on its own address, remove it from tools/remotes.json.

battery_low.title: {name}: battery at {level} %
battery_low.description: The battery of remote {name} is almost empty ({level} %). Put it in the dock or connect the charging cable. This notice disappears by itself once it charges or is above 20 %.

not_seen.title: {name} hasn't reported for {hours} hours
not_seen.description: Remote {name} last reported on {since}. Maybe the battery is empty, it is out of Wi-Fi and dock range, or it is lying somewhere. Press a key or put it in the dock. If you don't use this remote anymore, remove it under ESPHomeRemote → Configure – or ignore this notice.

not_seen_since_start.title: {name} hasn't reported for {hours} hours
not_seen_since_start.description: Remote {name} hasn't reported since Home Assistant started ({since}). Maybe the battery is empty, it is out of Wi-Fi and dock range, or it is lying somewhere. Press a key or put it in the dock. If you don't use this remote anymore, remove it under ESPHomeRemote → Configure – or ignore this notice.

no_supervisor.title: No ESPHome add-on: building and flashing from the configurator is unavailable
no_supervisor.description: This Home Assistant runs without Supervisor (Container or Core). Everything else works – key layouts, menu, dock, entities – but ESPHomeRemote cannot build or flash firmware for you. Build the device files in `{ordner}` with your own ESPHome (`esphome run` with the device file), or run Home Assistant OS / Supervised with the ESPHome add-on.

old_files.title: Old ESPHomeRemote files in the ESPHome folder

confirm.title: Move old files to the archive
confirm.description: Moves {dateien} to `esphome/archive/esphomeremote-alt-DATE/`. Devices and their settings are not affected; the next build uses the files from GitHub.

usb_flash_needed.title: {name}: flash once via USB
usb_flash_needed.description: {name} runs firmware {version}. Versions before 2026.11.5.4 need a new bootloader for the faster wake-up, and a bootloader cannot be updated over Wi-Fi. Connect the remote with a USB cable, open the configurator → Firmware → {name} → **USB** (Chrome or Edge). After that, updates over Wi-Fi work again.

flash_writes.title: {name}: unusually many flash writes
flash_writes.description: Remote {name} currently writes about {rate} times a day to its flash memory – normal is a few hundred (around {normal}). The memory lasts a very long time, but this rate points to a bug that saves something over and over. Please download the diagnostics (Settings → Devices & services → ESPHomeRemote → ⋮) and open an issue on GitHub. The notice disappears by itself once the rate is normal again.
